Task 4: IT/Facility Optimization – PUE Prediction (NREL) In Year 2, NREL made all of the PUE metrics available in Kafka and advanced the research into the energy balance. In addition, the initial development of PUE and energy balance models were completed. The next step in Year 3 will be to improve the robustness and efficacy of these models from initial development. This will come from verification of accuracy when comparing to current dashboard data streams, as well as from the inclusion of new hardware and metrics in these models. NREL’s next step in Year 3, from the efficacy standpoint, would be to develop, improve and complete a PUE prediction model. NREL Deliverables: • NREL will verify that the recently completed Energy Balance and PUE Models have ALL the needed metrics and data that should be included from the Druid database. • Develop, create and train a prediction model for PUE, which can more accurately predict the PUE based on input metrics, over time. • Investigate the efficacy of energy balance models for optimizing setpoints for IT equipment. • Work on the development of an anomaly detection dashboard for the energy balance of the complete data center, while monitoring streams of energy balance readings and sending alerts when any inflow or outflow energy readings from any of the facility or IT equipment’s are showing leaks, for additional investigation HPE Deliverables: • HPE will provide ongoing feedback on the different models and PUE prediction model, for possible improvements and increased robustness. 14 This report is available at no cost from NREL at www.nrel.gov/publications. Task 5: IT/Facility Optimization – Predictive Scheduling of Cooling (NREL) In Year 2, NREL has been able to classify application type and estimate the average power consumption for certain types of jobs – this ties in the Eagle jobs, power, and XALT data. Using this data, NREL has been able to calculate on a limited basis, the cooling system ramp time and correlated that to the application power usage. An initial test case for predictive ramp up/ramp down of the cooling system has been identified. An AI model strategy to predict the cooling system ramp time in advance of some significant power usage by a job was not completed in Year 2, so it has been rolled over into Year 3. NREL Deliverables: • Work with HPE to develop an AI model strategy to predict the cooling system ramp time • Create a dataset of metrics used to train the AI model • Integrate application profile information from Year 2 into SLURM for use in the AI model • Work with HPE to evaluate effectiveness of the power-aware prediction model for cooling system ramp up/ramp down time.
